$comment: Built on SIP — Memory Engine v0.2 receipt. Pluggable EmbeddingProvider + RRF hybrid search wired into RetrievalIndex (TypeScript / Node.js layer).
experiment: Add pluggable EmbeddingProvider interface to src/retrieval.ts. Two implementations: HashingTFProvider (zero deps, 1024-dim sparse, FNV-1a hash trick + TF·IDF + L2-norm) and TransformerProvider (optional peer dep @xenova/transformers, ONNX local, default model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 384-dim). RRF fusion (k=60, weights=[0.7 vec, 0.3 bm25]) wired as RetrievalIndex.hybridSearch(). Baseline: BM25-only RetrievalIndex.search().
implementationFiles: src/embedding.ts (new — 330 lines, EmbeddingProvider interface + HashingTFProvider + TransformerProvider + createEmbeddingProvider factory + rrfMerge)
src/retrieval.ts (modified — added setEmbeddingProvider, buildVectorIndex, hybridSearch, rankByVector, composeText; imports from embedding.ts)
package.json (modified — ./embedding export path, @xenova/transformers optional peer dep)
test/retrieval-embedding.test.ts (new — 17 tests, 16 pass, 1 skip [transformer, gated by STARLIGHT_EMBED=transformer])

providerChoice.rationale: @xenova/transformers is already widely used across the JS ecosystem, has broad model support (Hugging Face Hub), and the dynamic import pattern means it's a pure optional peer dep. fastembed has no sharp dependency (which is the usual win), but @xenova/transformers v2 also avoids sharp on the Node.js path when onnxruntime-node is preferred. The TransformerProvider implementation uses dynamic specifier import to prevent tsc from resolving the optional dep at compile time — CI stays green without the package.

measurements.environment: Windows 11, Node 20.20.2, public-vault corpus (108 entries, 10 labeled queries from test/retrieval-eval.test.ts)
measurements.provider: HashingTFProvider (zero deps, no model download — CI-reproducible)

hashingTF_hybridSearch.note: Same labeled query set and corpus as retrieval-eval.test.ts BM25-only baseline. HashingTF hybrid matches or equals BM25 on this small 108-entry corpus.

bm25Baseline.note: From test/retrieval-eval.test.ts, same corpus. BM25 is already perfect on this small public-vault corpus; hybrid cannot improve on a ceiling.

transformerProvider.status: PENDING — @xenova/transformers not installed in this environment
transformerProvider.expectedGain: Based on Python harness (2026-06-10, tools/proving-ground/scorecards/2026-06-10-memory-lane-rrf-hybrid.json): RRF hybrid achieved +61% precision@10 lift over lexical-only on the 520-atom eval-50 corpus. The TypeScript port uses the same RRF formula (k=60, weights=[0.7, 0.3]) and should reproduce that gain when measured against eval-50.jsonl with a real embedding model.
transformerProvider.howToMeasure: STARLIGHT_EMBED=transformer node --import tsx --test test/retrieval-embedding.test.ts (after installing @xenova/transformers, model downloads on first run to ~/.cache)

testResults.npm_test: 981 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (transformer gated), 7 todo — all existing tests green

designDecisions.rrfWeights: [0.7 vector, 0.3 bm25] — proved optimal in Python harness 2026-06-10; configurable via rrfWeights option
designDecisions.rrfK: 60 — standard RRF constant; configurable via rrfK option
designDecisions.fallback: hybridSearch() falls back to search() (BM25-only) when vector index is empty
designDecisions.gracefulDegradation: TransformerProvider.embed() returns [] (empty vector) on any error; similarity() returns 0 for empty vectors
designDecisions.ciSafety: TransformerProvider gated by STARLIGHT_EMBED=transformer env var; no model download in CI; HashingTFProvider is the default (zero new deps)
designDecisions.jsonlCanonUntouched: JSONL files are not modified; RetrievalIndex is a sidecar index only
designDecisions.vectorIndexLifecycle: rebuildFromVaults() clears vectorIndex; caller must re-call buildVectorIndex() for hybrid search after rebuild

weakness: The public-vault corpus (108 entries) is too small and lexically clean for the hybrid path to show improvement over BM25. The real measurement surface is eval-50.jsonl (520-atom corpus, 50 queries) where the Python harness proved +61% precision@10. That measurement requires the transformer provider and is PENDING in this environment. The labeled query set in retrieval-eval.test.ts should grow beyond n=10 to make recall@k claims statistically meaningful.
nextExperiments: Install @xenova/transformers, run STARLIGHT_EMBED=transformer npm run eval:retrieval — measure hybrid vs BM25 on the 10-query public-vault set
Port eval-50.jsonl to a TypeScript harness so the 520-atom / 50-query measurement is reproducible in npm test (currently Python-only)
Add a semantic ground-truth eval (LLM-judged relevance) — the lexical token-overlap judge structurally under-credits the semantic channel
antiGoodhart: These numbers describe the system under HashingTF on a 108-entry corpus. Do not optimize to them; the load-bearing measurement is eval-50 with a transformer provider.
